facts.statement: Kourisodon is an extinct genus of mosasaur named after its Greek meaning of "razor tooth".
facts.quote: Kourisodon (from the Greek κουρίς kourís + ὀδών odon, "razor tooth") is an extinct genus of mosasaur.

facts.statement: Kourisodon was first classified in the tribe Leiodontini but is now classified as a clidastine.
facts.quote: Kourisodon was originally described as a member of the "Leiodontini", more recently as a "Clidastine".

facts.statement: Fossils of Kourisodon have been found on Vancouver Island in Canada and in the Izumi Group of Japan.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada, as well as from the Izumi Group of Japan.

facts.statement: Kourisodon fossils date from the Late Santonian stage to the Late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: These finds date back to the late Santonian stage and the late Campanian to the late Maastrichtian, respectively, of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The type species K. puntledgensis was a small mosasaur reaching an estimated length of about 3.75 meters.
facts.quote: K. puntledgensis was a small mosasaur, with an estimated length of about 3.75 meters (around 12.3 feet).

facts.statement: K. puntledgensis lived in a Pacific environment alongside elasmosaurids, turtles, and other mosasaurs, but no polycotylids were present.
facts.quote: It shared its environment with a variety of Elasmosaurids, turtles, and other mosasaurs, although it seems that no polycotylids were present in its Pacific environment.

facts.statement: A fragmentary skeleton from Shikoku Island, Japan, found in 2005 was assigned to an unnamed species of Kourisodon.
facts.quote: In 2005, a fragmentary skeleton from exposures of the Izumi Group on Shikoku Island, Japan, was assigned to Kourisodon sp.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that a Japanese specimen with longer maxillary teeth might represent a second, unnamed species of Kourisodon.
facts.quote: This specimen demonstrated longer maxillary teeth among other differences from K. puntledgensis, which the authors interpreted to mean that this individual belonged to a second species, although this new species has not yet been formally named.

facts.statement: A complete 12-foot-3-inch replica of the type specimen is displayed at the Canadian Fossil Discovery Centre in Manitoba.
facts.quote: A 12' 3" complete replica of the Puntledge River specimen is on display at the Canadian Fossil Discovery Centre in Morden, Manitoba.

facts.statement: Kourisodon belongs to the subfamily Mosasaurinae within the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Mosasauroidea familia: Mosasauridae † subfamilia: Mosasaurinae

facts.statement: Kourisodon lived between 85.7 and 66 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to Maastrichtian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus Kourisodon was formally described by Nicholls and Meckert in 2002.
rejected.quote: Kourisodon (from the Greek κουρίς kourís + ὀδών odon, "razor tooth") is an extinct genus of mosasaur.
